Writes the bytes the lowercase hex constant `text` spells at `out[at]` and answers where they end: how this stack's fixed values, written out where they are defined, become bytes without an array of their own.

<scalar-card title="tlsListHas" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlslisthas">

<scalar-card title="tlsParseClientHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsparseclienthello">

Reads the ClientHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — the message without its four-byte handshake header — into a fresh `TlsClientHello`, with `tlsReadClientHello`'s checks and its `alert`, every field copied out.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadCertificate" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadcertificate">

Reads a server's Certificate body (§4.4.2) into `view`: the request context's length, which the client requires to be 0, and the list of entries.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadCertificateVerify" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadcertificateverify">

Reads a CertificateVerify body (§4.4.3) into `view`: the scheme and the signature.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadClientHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadclienthello">

Reads the ClientHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — the message without its four-byte handshake header — into `hello`, which forgets the last one first.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadEncryptedExtensions" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadencryptedextensions">

Reads an EncryptedExtensions body (§4.3.1) into `view`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadNewSessionTicket" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadnewsessionticket">

Checks a NewSessionTicket body's structure (§4.6.1) into `view`'s `alert`: the client keeps no tickets, so it reads one only to discard it, but a malformed one is still `decode_error`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadServerHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadserverhello">

Reads the ServerHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — without its handshake header — into `view`, which tells a HelloRetryRequest from it by its `random` (§4.1.3).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsSelectPskIdentity" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsselectpskidentity">

Points `hello`'s `pskIdentity*`, `pskTicketAge` and `pskBinder*` at the offer's identity number `index` and the binder of the same number, and answers whether there is one: false for an index out of range, or a hello that offered no `pre_shared_key` or did not parse.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsServerHelloDowngrade" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsserverhellodowngrade">

Whether the ServerHello in `view` carries a downgrade sentinel in the last 8 bytes of its random (§4.1.3), which a TLS 1.3 client must refuse with `illegal_parameter`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWindowHasU16" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswindowhasu16">

Whether the 16-bit values `data[at .. at + length)` hold `value`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWindowString" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswindowstring">

The bytes of `data[at .. at + length)` as a string of one character a byte: ASCII here, a host name.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteCertificate" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritecertificate">

Writes a server's Certificate (§4.4.2) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: an empty request context, then each DER certificate of `chain`, leaf first, with no extensions of its own.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteCertificateVerify" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritecertificateverify">

Writes a CertificateVerify (§4.4.3) at `out[at]`: the signature scheme and the signature as it goes on the wire.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteCertificateVerifyContent" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritecertificateverifycontent">

Writes what a server's CertificateVerify signs (§4.4.3) at `out[at]`: 64 spaces, the context string "TLS 1.3, server CertificateVerify", a zero byte, and the transcript hash `transcriptHash[off .. off + len)` through Certificate.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteClientHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswriteclienthello">

Writes a ClientHello (§4.1.2) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: `random`, the `legacy_session_id` `sessionId`, the cipher suites `suites`, null compression, then the extensions `server_name` (a `host_name`, left out when `serverName` is empty), `supported_groups` (`groups`), `signature_algorithms`, ALPN (left out when `alpn` is empty), `supported_versions` (TLS 1.3 alone), a `key_share` with the one entry `shareGroup`/`sharePublic`, and `cookie` when `cookie` is not empty (the echo of a HelloRetryRequest's, §4.2.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteEncryptedExtensions" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswriteencryptedextensions">

Writes EncryptedExtensions (§4.3.1) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteFinished" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritefinished">

Writes a Finished (§4.4.4) at `out[at]`, carrying `verifyData[off .. off + len)`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteHelloRetryRequest" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritehelloretryrequest">

Writes a HelloRetryRequest (§4.1.4) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: a ServerHello whose `random` is the fixed HelloRetryRequest value, choosing `suite`, echoing the session id, and asking for a share of `group` in `key_share`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteNewSessionTicket" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritenewsessionticket">

Writes a NewSessionTicket (§4.6.1) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: `lifetime` in seconds, `ageAdd`, the nonce `nonce[nonceOff .. nonceOff + nonceLength)`, the ticket `ticket[ticketOff .. ticketOff + ticketLength)`, and `extra` as the extensions, encoded by the caller and written as they are.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteServerHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswriteserverhello">

Writes a ServerHello (§4.1.3) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: choosing `suite` and TLS 1.3, echoing the session id `sessionId[sessionIdOff .. sessionIdOff + sessionIdLength)`, and carrying the server's x25519 share.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteServerHelloPsk" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswriteserverhellopsk">

Writes the ServerHello of a resumed handshake (§4.1.3, §4.2.11) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: `tlsWriteServerHello`'s, with a `pre_shared_key` that names the client's identity number `selectedIdentity` (a `uint16`) ahead of `key_share`, since the server resumes only in `psk_dhe_ke` and so always sends its share.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TlsClientHello" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsclienthello">

A ClientHello as `tlsParseClientHello` read it (RFC 8446 §4.1.2), each field copied out of the message into an array of its own: the same hello as a `TlsClientHelloView`, for a caller that wants values rather than windows.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TlsClientHelloView" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsclienthelloview">

A ClientHello as `tlsReadClientHello` read it, without a byte copied: every field the server needs is a window `(…At, …Length)` into `data`, the buffer the hello was read from, and the rest are numbers and flags.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TlsServerFlightView" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsserverflightview">

One message of the server's flight as a `tlsRead*` function below read it: a ServerHello or HelloRetryRequest, EncryptedExtensions, Certificate, CertificateVerify or NewSessionTicket.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

One reader and eight writers. `tlsParseClientHello` reads a ClientHello body
into a `TlsClientHello`, checking its structure: every length against the
bytes it claims, every vector against its RFC 8446 bounds, and no extension
twice (§4.2). A message that breaks one answers the alert a server sends for
it in the hello's `alert` field (`decode_error` for a malformed or truncated
one, `illegal_parameter` for a duplicate), never a panic, since every byte
of it is the peer's. What the fields *mean* — which version, which suite,
whether a share is missing — is the server's to decide, in `nish/net/tls`.

</scalar-callout>

`tlsReadClientHello` is the same reader for a server that keeps its state
in a slot: it reads into a `TlsClientHelloView` made once, whose fields are
windows into the message rather than copies of it, so a ClientHello read
allocates nothing, and `tlsParseClientHello` copies a view's windows out.

The writers each answer one whole handshake message, header included:
ServerHello, a resumed ServerHello that names the PSK it accepts,
HelloRetryRequest, EncryptedExtensions, Certificate, CertificateVerify,
Finished and NewSessionTicket. Their inputs come from the server and the
caller's configuration rather than from the peer, so they check nothing.
Each is a `tlsWrite*` function that writes into the caller's array at an
offset — run over an empty array, it measures — and a `tlsEncode*` one
that answers the message in a fresh array.

The client's side is the mirror: `tlsWriteClientHello` and
`tlsEncodeClientHello` write the hello `nish/net/tls/client` sends, and five
readers — `tlsReadServerHello` (a HelloRetryRequest too),
`tlsReadEncryptedExtensions`, `tlsReadCertificate`,
`tlsReadCertificateVerify` and `tlsReadNewSessionTicket` — read the
server's flight into a `TlsServerFlightView` made once, as windows, with
the same checks and the same alerts in its `alert` field. A server's bytes
are the peer's just as a client's are, so these readers never panic either
(the `tls-server-flight` fuzz target).

The extensions read are `server_name` (RFC 6066 §3), `supported_groups`,
`signature_algorithms`, `supported_versions` and `key_share` (RFC 8446
§4.2), `application_layer_protocol_negotiation` (RFC 7301 §3.1) and
`quic_transport_parameters` (RFC 9001 §8.2), and `pre_shared_key` and
`psk_key_exchange_modes` (RFC 8446 §4.2.11, §4.2.9), whose identities and
binders the reader checks against their syntax but does not open: a ticket
and its binder are the server's to judge. Every other extension is skipped,
which is what RFC 8446 §4.2 asks of a server that does not know it.

Written from the RFCs, not ported from another implementation. Private
names carry the `tls` prefix because a `std/` module's private functions
share the importing program's flat symbol namespace (`docs/wp26-stdlib.md`
§3e).

## tlsParseClientHello

Reads the ClientHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — the message without

## tlsReadCertificate

Reads a server's Certificate body (§4.4.2) into `view`: the request
context's length, which the client requires to be 0, and the list of
entries. An empty list is `decode_error`, as §4.4.2.4 has a client answer
it; an entry with extensions is `unsupported_extension`, because the
client offers none that a CertificateEntry may carry.

```ts
function tlsReadCertificate(
  view: TlsServerFlightView,
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): void
```

## tlsReadClientHello

Reads the ClientHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — the message without
its four-byte handshake header — into `hello`, which forgets the last one
first. Its `alert` is 0 when the body parsed; otherwise the first fault
decides it: `decode_error` for a length past its bytes, a vector out of its
bounds or bytes left over, and `illegal_parameter` for an extension sent
twice (§4.2), a `pre_shared_key` that is not the last extension (§4.2.11),
two shares for one group, or a bad `server_name`. A window outside `data`
is `decode_error` too, rather than a panic. A hello that parses but offers
`pre_shared_key` with a different number of identities and binders is
`illegal_parameter`, and one that offers it without
`psk_key_exchange_modes` is `missing_extension` (§4.2.9): rows 10 to 13 of
the fallback table in `docs/security/tls.md`, "Resumption". Nothing is copied: the windows
point into `data`, which must outlive the use made of them.

```ts
function tlsReadClientHello(
  hello: TlsClientHelloView,
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hello" type="TlsClientHelloView" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

Points `hello`'s `pskIdentity*`, `pskTicketAge` and `pskBinder*` at the
offer's identity number `index` and the binder of the same number, and
answers whether there is one: false for an index out of range, or a hello

## tlsWriteClientHello

Writes a ClientHello (§4.1.2) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends:
`random`, the `legacy_session_id` `sessionId`, the cipher suites `suites`,
null compression, then the extensions `server_name` (a `host_name`, left
out when `serverName` is empty), `supported_groups` (`groups`),
`signature_algorithms`, ALPN (left out when `alpn` is empty),
`supported_versions` (TLS 1.3 alone), a `key_share` with the one entry
`shareGroup`/`sharePublic`, and `cookie` when `cookie` is not empty (the
echo of a HelloRetryRequest's, §4.2.2).

## TlsClientHello

A ClientHello as `tlsParseClientHello` read it (RFC 8446 §4.1.2), each field
copied out of the message into an array of its own: the same hello as a
`TlsClientHelloView`, for a caller that wants values rather than windows. A
field whose extension was absent keeps its empty value, and its `has*` flag
says so.

```ts
class TlsClientHello
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsClientHello()` |  |
| `alert: i32` | 0 when the message parsed, or the alert it earns: `decode_error` or `illegal_parameter`. |
| `alpn: u8[][]` | The ALPN protocol names offered, each as its bytes (RFC 7301 §3.1). |
| `cipherSuites: i32[]` |  |
| `extensionTypes: i32[]` | Every extension type read, in order. |
| `groups: i32[]` | `supported_groups`, in the client's order. |
| `hasAlpn: boolean` |  |
| `hasKeyShare: boolean` |  |
| `hasPreSharedKey: boolean` |  |
| `hasPskModes: boolean` |  |
| `hasQuicTransportParameters: boolean` |  |
| `hasServerName: boolean` |  |
| `hasSignatureAlgorithms: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedGroups: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedVersions: boolean` |  |
| `hasX25519Share: boolean` |  |
| `legacyVersion: i32` |  |
| `nullCompressionOnly: boolean` | Whether `legacy_compression_methods` is the single null method TLS 1.3 requires (§4.1.2). |
| `pskBinders: u8[][]` | `pre_shared_key`'s binders, one an identity. |
| `pskBindersPrefix: i32` | How many bytes of the body come before `binders`: the body truncated there, after its handshake header, is what each binder covers (§4.2.11.2). |
| `pskDheKe: boolean` | Whether `psk_key_exchange_modes` lists `psk_dhe_ke`. |
| `pskIdentities: u8[][]` | `pre_shared_key`'s identities, in the client's order, and each one's obfuscated ticket age (§4.2.11). |
| `pskModes: u8[]` | `psk_key_exchange_modes`, one byte a mode. |
| `pskTicketAges: u32[]` |  |
| `quicTransportParameters: u8[]` | The client's `quic_transport_parameters`, opaque (RFC 9001 §8.2). |
| `random: u8[]` |  |
| `serverName: string` | The `host_name` of `server_name`, or empty. |
| `sessionId: u8[]` | `legacy_session_id`, which a server echoes (§4.1.3). |
| `shareGroups: i32[]` | Every group a key share was offered for, in order. |
| `signatureSchemes: i32[]` | `signature_algorithms`, in the client's order. |
| `versions: i32[]` | `supported_versions`, in the client's order. |
| `x25519Share: u8[]` | The x25519 share's key_exchange, as sent; its length is the server's to check. |

## TlsClientHelloView

A ClientHello as `tlsReadClientHello` read it, without a byte copied: every
field the server needs is a window `(…At, …Length)` into `data`, the buffer
the hello was read from, and the rest are numbers and flags. A field whose
extension was absent keeps an empty window, and its `has*` flag says so,
since an empty list and a missing extension mean different things to the
server (§9.2). Make one per connection and read every hello into it: it
allocates nothing after its constructor, so a handshake that keeps its state
in a slot reads its ClientHellos without moving the arena.

```ts
class TlsClientHelloView
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsClientHelloView()` |  |
| `alert: i32` | 0 when the message parsed, or the alert it earns: `decode_error` or `illegal_parameter`. |
| `alpnAt: i32` | ALPN's `protocol_name_list`, each name a length byte and its bytes (RFC 7301 §3.1). |
| `alpnLength: i32` |  |
| `data: u8[]` | The buffer the windows point into: the one the last hello was read from. |
| `extensionsAt: i32` | The extensions block, every extension in it. |
| `extensionSeen: u32[]` | One bit per extension type read, for the duplicate check (§4.2); cleared by each read. |
| `extensionsLength: i32` |  |
| `groupsAt: i32` | `supported_groups`, 16-bit values. |
| `groupsLength: i32` |  |
| `hasAlpn: boolean` |  |
| `hasKeyShare: boolean` |  |
| `hasPreSharedKey: boolean` |  |
| `hasPskModes: boolean` |  |
| `hasQuicTransportParameters: boolean` |  |
| `hasServerName: boolean` |  |
| `hasSignatureAlgorithms: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedGroups: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedVersions: boolean` |  |
| `hasX25519Share: boolean` |  |
| `legacyVersion: i32` |  |
| `nullCompressionOnly: boolean` | Whether `legacy_compression_methods` is the single null method TLS 1.3 requires (§4.1.2). |
| `pskBinderAt: i32` | That identity's binder, the entry of the same index in `binders`. |
| `pskBinderCount: i32` |  |
| `pskBinderLength: i32` |  |
| `pskBindersAt: i32` | `pre_shared_key`'s `binders` list: each a PskBinderEntry<32..255>. |
| `pskBindersLength: i32` |  |
| `pskBindersPrefixAt: i32` | Where `binders`' two-byte length starts: the ClientHello up to here, its handshake header included, is what each binder is computed over (§4.2.11.2). |

| `pskIdentityLength: i32` |  |
| `pskModesAt: i32` | `psk_key_exchange_modes`' `ke_modes`, one byte a mode (§4.2.9). |
| `pskModesLength: i32` |  |
| `pskTicketAge: u32` |  |
| `quicAt: i32` | The client's `quic_transport_parameters`, opaque (RFC 9001 §8.2). |
| `quicLength: i32` |  |

## TlsServerFlightView

One message of the server's flight as a `tlsRead*` function below read it:
a ServerHello or HelloRetryRequest, EncryptedExtensions, Certificate,
CertificateVerify or NewSessionTicket. Like `TlsClientHelloView` its fields
are windows into `data` and numbers, so a read allocates nothing; each read
forgets the last message first.

Two verdicts, kept apart so the client can rank them. `alert` is the
structure's: `decode_error` for a length past its bytes, a vector out of
its bounds or bytes left over. `extensionAlert` is the extensions': an
extension sent twice, or one the client offered but this message may not
carry, is `illegal_parameter`; one the client never offers is
`unsupported_extension` (§4.2). The client reads the structure first, then
the version and the downgrade sentinel, then the extensions, so that a
TLS 1.2 ServerHello is refused for its version, not for the extensions a
TLS 1.2 server sends.

```ts
class TlsServerFlightView
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsServerFlightView()` |  |
| `alert: i32` | 0 when the message parsed, else `decode_error`. |
| `alpnAt: i32` | EncryptedExtensions' ALPN: the one protocol the server chose (RFC 7301 §3.1). |
| `alpnLength: i32` |  |
| `certificateCount: i32` |  |
| `certificatesAt: i32` | Certificate's `certificate_list`, every entry in it, and how many there are. |
| `certificatesLength: i32` |  |
| `compression: i32` |  |
| `contextLength: i32` | Certificate's `certificate_request_context`, which must be empty for a server's (§4.4.2). |
| `cookieAt: i32` | A HelloRetryRequest's `cookie`, which the second ClientHello echoes (§4.2.2). |
| `cookieLength: i32` |  |
| `data: u8[]` | The buffer the windows point into: the one the last message was read from. |
| `extensionAlert: i32` | 0 when the extensions are ones this message may carry, else `illegal_parameter` or `unsupported_extension`. |
| `extensionSeen: u32[]` | One bit per extension type read, for the duplicate check (§4.2). |
| `hasAlpn: boolean` |  |
| `hasCookie: boolean` |  |
| `hasKeyShare: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedVersions: boolean` |  |
| `isRetry: boolean` | A ServerHello whose `random` is the HelloRetryRequest value (§4.1.3). |
| `legacyVersion: i32` |  |
| `randomAt: i32` |  |
| `reader: TlsReader` | The reader each read runs, kept so that a read allocates none. |
| `scheme: i32` | CertificateVerify's scheme and signature (§4.4.3). |
| `selectedVersion: i32` |  |
| `serverNameAcknowledged: boolean` | EncryptedExtensions' empty `server_name`, the acknowledgement of RFC 6066 §3. |
| `sessionIdAt: i32` |  |

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`TLS_HANDSHAKE_CLIENT_HELLO: i32`

`nish/net/tls/codec` — the TLS 1.3 handshake messages a server and a
client read and write (RFC 8446 §4), as bytes.

One reader and eight writers. `tlsParseClientHello` reads a ClientHello body
into a `TlsClientHello`, checking its structure: every length against the
bytes it claims, every vector against its RFC 8446 bounds, and no extension
twice (§4.2). A message that breaks one answers the alert a server sends for
it in the hello's `alert` field (`decode_error` for a malformed or truncated
one, `illegal_parameter` for a duplicate), never a panic, since every byte
of it is the peer's. What the fields *mean* — which version, which suite,
whether a share is missing — is the server's to decide, in `nish/net/tls`.

`tlsReadClientHello` is the same reader for a server that keeps its state
in a slot: it reads into a `TlsClientHelloView` made once, whose fields are
windows into the message rather than copies of it, so a ClientHello read
allocates nothing, and `tlsParseClientHello` copies a view's windows out.

The writers each answer one whole handshake message, header included:
ServerHello, a resumed ServerHello that names the PSK it accepts,
HelloRetryRequest, EncryptedExtensions, Certificate, CertificateVerify,
Finished and NewSessionTicket. Their inputs come from the server and the
caller's configuration rather than from the peer, so they check nothing.
Each is a `tlsWrite*` function that writes into the caller's array at an
offset — run over an empty array, it measures — and a `tlsEncode*` one
that answers the message in a fresh array.

The client's side is the mirror: `tlsWriteClientHello` and
`tlsEncodeClientHello` write the hello `nish/net/tls/client` sends, and five
readers — `tlsReadServerHello` (a HelloRetryRequest too),
`tlsReadEncryptedExtensions`, `tlsReadCertificate`,
`tlsReadCertificateVerify` and `tlsReadNewSessionTicket` — read the
server's flight into a `TlsServerFlightView` made once, as windows, with
the same checks and the same alerts in its `alert` field. A server's bytes
are the peer's just as a client's are, so these readers never panic either
(the `tls-server-flight` fuzz target).

The extensions read are `server_name` (RFC 6066 §3), `supported_groups`,
`signature_algorithms`, `supported_versions` and `key_share` (RFC 8446
§4.2), `application_layer_protocol_negotiation` (RFC 7301 §3.1) and
`quic_transport_parameters` (RFC 9001 §8.2), and `pre_shared_key` and
`psk_key_exchange_modes` (RFC 8446 §4.2.11, §4.2.9), whose identities and
binders the reader checks against their syntax but does not open: a ticket
and its binder are the server's to judge. Every other extension is skipped,
which is what RFC 8446 §4.2 asks of a server that does not know it.

Written from the RFCs, not ported from another implementation. Private
names carry the `tls` prefix because a `std/` module's private functions
share the importing program's flat symbol namespace (`docs/wp26-stdlib.md`
§3e).

</scalar-card>
